questions.question: Let $A = \left( \begin{matrix}0 & 1 & 2 \\ a & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & c & 0\end{matrix} \right)$, where $a,c \in R$. If ${A}^{3} = A$ and the positive value of $a$ belongs to the interval $(n - 1,n]$, where $n \in ℕ$, then $n$ is equal to ____.

Given,

Now finding,

${A}^{3} = \left( \begin{matrix}a + 2 & 2c & 3 \\ 3 & a + 3c & 2a \\ ca & 1 & 2 + 3c\end{matrix} \right)\left( \begin{matrix}0 & 1 & 2 \\ a & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & c & 0\end{matrix} \right) \implies {A}^{3} = \left( \begin{matrix}2ca + 3 & \alpha + 2 + 3c & 2a + 4 + 6c \\ {a}^{2} + 3ca + 2a & 3 + 2ac & 6 + 3a + 9c \\ a + 2 + 3c & ca + 2c + 3{c}^{2} & 2ca + 3\end{matrix} \right)$

Now equating ${A}^{3} = A$ and comparing both side we get,

$2ca + 3 = 0 \implies c = \frac{ - 3}{2a}$

And $a + 2 + 3c = 1 \implies a + 2 + 3\left(\frac{ - 3}{2a}\right) = 1 \implies a + 1 - \frac{9}{2a} = 0 \implies 2{a}^{2} + 2a - 9 = 0 \implies a = \frac{ - 2 + \sqrt{4 + 4 \times 9 \times 2}}{4} = \frac{ - 2 + \sqrt{76}}{4} \approx \frac{6.7}{4} \approx 1.4$

Hence, $a \in (1,2]$

So, on comparing with $a \in (n - 1,n]$ we get $n = 2$

questions.question:
Consider the matrix $f\left(x\right) = \left( \begin{matrix}\cos x & - \sin x & 0 \\ \sin x & \cos x & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{matrix} \right)$. Given below are two statements :

Hence statement-I is correct

Now, checking statement II

$\implies f\left(y\right) = \left( \begin{matrix}\cos y & - \sin y & 0 \\ \sin y & \cos y & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{matrix} \right) \implies f\left(x\right)f\left(y\right) = \left( \begin{matrix}\cos x & - \sin x & 0 \\ \sin x & \cos x & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{matrix} \right)\left( \begin{matrix}\cos y & - \sin y & 0 \\ \sin y & \cos y & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{matrix} \right) \implies f\left(x\right)f\left(y\right) = \left( \begin{matrix}\cos x\cos y - \sin x\sin y & - \cos x\sin y - \sin x\cos y & 0 \\ \sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y & - \sin x\sin y + \cos x\cos y & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{matrix} \right) \implies f\left(x\right)f\left(y\right) = \left( \begin{matrix}\cos (x + y) & - \sin (x + y) & 0 \\ \sin (x + y) & \cos (x + y) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{matrix} \right) \implies f(x) \cdot f(y) = f(x + y)$

questions.question: Let $A = \left( \begin{matrix}2 & 3 \\ a & 0\end{matrix} \right),a \in R$ be written as $P + Q$ where $P$ is a symmetric matrix and $Q$ is skew symmetric matrix. If $det\left(Q\right) = 9$, then the modulus of the sum of all possible values of determinant of $P$ is equal to:
questions.explanation:
We have,

$A = \left( \begin{matrix}2 & 3 \\ a & 0\end{matrix} \right),a \in R$

Then,

${A}^{T} = \left( \begin{matrix}2 & a \\ 3 & 0\end{matrix} \right)$

Now,

$P = \left(\frac{A + {A}^{T}}{2}\right) \implies P = \frac{1}{2}\left(\left( \begin{matrix}2 & 3 \\ a & 0\end{matrix} \right) + \left( \begin{matrix}2 & a \\ 3 & 0\end{matrix} \right)\right) \implies P = \left( \begin{matrix}2 & \frac{3 + a}{2} \\ \frac{a + 3}{2} & 0\end{matrix} \right)$

And,

$Q = \frac{A - {A}^{T}}{2} \implies Q = \frac{1}{2}\left(\left( \begin{matrix}2 & 3 \\ a & 0\end{matrix} \right) - \left( \begin{matrix}2 & a \\ 3 & 0\end{matrix} \right)\right) \implies Q = \left( \begin{matrix}0 & \frac{3 - a}{2} \\ \frac{a - 3}{2} & 0\end{matrix} \right)$

As,

$det(Q) = 9 \implies {\left(a - 3\right)}^{2} = 36 \implies a = 3 \pm 6 ∴a = 9, - 3$

Now,

$det\left(P\right) = - {\left(\frac{3 + a}{2}\right)}^{2}$

For $a = - 3,det\left(P\right) = 0$

For $a = 9$, $det\left(P\right) = - {\left(\frac{3 + 9}{2}\right)}^{2} = - 36 ∴$ Modulus of the sum of all possible values of $\det \left(P\right) = \left( - 36\right) + \left(0\right) = 36$
